question.text: A particle is moving in a straight line such that its velocity is increasing at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> per meter. The acceleration of the particle is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> at a point where its velocity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.

solution.text:
According to the question, velocity is increasing at 5 m s-1. Therefore, dvds=5 s-1. 

Now acceleration a=dvdt=vdvds

⇒a=vdvds=20×5=100 m s-2
